column1:
General note on food information
The Australian Food Composition Database includes a core set of nutrients for all foods. As such, there is a small amount of data across all categories which have been imputed, borrowed or estimated to fill data gaps for core nutrients, where required. Further information on the source of nutrient data for all foods is available in the Sampling Details field of Release 3 - Food Details.

Profiles are generally derived by nutrient analysis with some recipes for common homemade dishes. Specific attention was given to sodium, fat and fatty acid content with a substantial amount of analysis taking place in 2008/09 and again in 2013.

Resistant starch is reported for a number of cereal and grain products based on analyses by Goodman Fielder, Grain Growers Ltd and Ingredion ANZ Pty Ltd in 2012.

For some cereal products, particularly low-moisture baked products such as biscuits and breakfast cereals, the sum of proximates (macronutrients) is below generally acceptable levels for food composition tables (less than 95 g/100 g). This is likely to reflect problems with the analysis of starch and/or dietary fibre in these foods.
